_about: Embraer ERJ-140 (EMB-135KE/KL), built from the EMB-145's snapped lines (e145/, Figure 2.2.1 of APM-145/1100) with the two plugs the ERJ-140's own Airport Planning Manual gives taken out (plug.py on e145's *.snap.json, as the 777-8 from the 777-9): APM-145/1521, Revision 8 (Nov 29/24), 2.2 Airplane Dimensions (page index 17: fuselage 26.51 m, overall 28.45 m), Figure 2.2.1 (page index 18: nose to main gear 13.53 m) and Figure 2.7.1 Door Clearances (page index 27-28). 0.91 m at 9.0 m from the nose (ahead of the wing: the nose-to-main-gear 13.53 m against the EMB-145's 14.44 m) and 0.51 m at 18.0 m (behind it: the rest of the 1.42 m). The baggage door then sits at 21.09 m (Figure 2.7.1: 21.12 m). Not snapped to the ERJ-140's own figure: its views aren't to one scale (the side 5.2% and the plan 3.9% short lengthwise against their spans and the front view, the side drawn 1.41 degrees nose down), and evened out they still put the main door 0.26 m aft of the printed 4.90 m and draw 9 windows ahead of the overwing exit. Its door figure prints the exit 12.79 m from the nose, the ERJ-135's figure (the two manuals share the sheet). Side-on photos of ERJ-140s (Wikimedia Commons: N823AE, CFIF, public domain; N820AE, Aeroprints.com, CC BY-SA 3.0, right side) show 10 windows ahead of the exit and 5 behind it, the EMB-145's 11 and 6 less one in each plug, and N823AE's exit about 13.9 m from the nose (scaled by its 26.51 m): the plugs' 13.86 m. Windows, doors and cockpit panes are the EMB-145's, moved by the plugs (one window in each plug dropped). Rebuild: e140/derive.py (the EMB-145's work directory to this one), then build.py and smooth.py.

sources.title: Embraer, ERJ-140 Airport Planning Manual (APM-145/1521, Revision 8, Nov 29/24), 2.2 Airplane Dimensions, Figure 2.2.1 Airplane General Dimensions, Figure 2.7.1 Door Clearances
sources.note: The fuselage, overall length and nose-to-main-gear figures give the two plugs taken out of the EMB-145's measured lines (tools/trace/e140/); the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. Figure 2.2.1 isn't drawn to one scale and isn't used for the outlines; its door figure's 12.79 m to the overwing exit is the ERJ-135's (the photos and the plugs put it at 13.86 m).
